Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

Behavioral health professional with experience across ABA, child welfare, and healthcare, bringing a strong foundation in client support, staff development, program coordination, and safety-focused practices. Skilled in training and supporting team members, coordinating with families and multidisciplinary professionals, maintaining accurate documentation, and managing competing priorities in fast-paced environments. Experienced in responding to behavioral challenges, navigating sensitive situations, and promoting consistency and accountability in service delivery. Holds a master’s degree in Special Education with an ABA concentration and a graduate certificate in Contemporary Theory in Mental Health Services, and is pursuing a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a concentration in child and adolescent counseling. Passionate about supporting effective program operations and creating structured, compassionate environments where adolescents and their families can thrive, while ensuring staff feel supported, empowered, and equipped to provide quality care.

Cover Letter: 

Dear Hiring Team,

I was excited to come across the Program Operations Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy because it brings together several areas that have shaped my professional experience and career goals: behavioral health, team development, and supporting children and families. Through my work in ABA and child welfare, I have seen how much of a difference a well-organized, supportive environment can make in a young person's progress. I would love the opportunity to build on that experience by helping lead a program where compassionate care, clear expectations, and strong daily operations work together to support adolescents and their families.

Throughout my nearly five years in ABA, I have gained hands-on experience supporting children and families while helping ensure treatment programs are implemented consistently and effectively. In my role as a Student Analyst, I participated in client intakes and initial assessments, contributed to reassessments and treatment planning, reviewed clinical documentation and behavioral data, and supported parent training and collaboration with multidisciplinary providers. I also helped train and support RBTs, communicate expectations, and work through challenges that affected treatment implementation. These responsibilities taught me the importance of clear communication, staff accountability, consistency, and attention to detail, all of which I recognize as essential to managing daily operations in a PHP/IOP setting.

My experience as a Child Protective Investigator with the State of Florida further strengthened my ability to respond calmly to challenging situations, gather and document sensitive information, assess safety concerns, and communicate with families experiencing difficult circumstances. This role required sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to navigate competing priorities while remaining focused on the well-being of children. I believe these skills would translate well to supporting adolescents with behavioral and emotional needs, responding to unexpected challenges, and helping maintain a safe, structured program environment.

I also bring experience in healthcare administration, including insurance verification, client communication, and managing responsibilities in a fast-paced environment. Combined with my clinical documentation and coordination experience, this background has prepared me to approach operational responsibilities with organization, follow-through, and an understanding of how administrative processes affect the overall client experience. I understand that effective program operations require more than keeping schedules and tasks on track. They require a team that communicates well, understands expectations, follows established procedures, and works together to provide consistent care to clients and their families. I value creating a workplace where staff feel supported and equipped to succeed while also understanding the importance of accountability, collaboration, and maintaining high standards of care.

My educational background reflects my continued commitment to understanding and supporting children, adolescents, and families. I hold a master's degree in Special Education with a concentration in Applied Behavior Analysis, a graduate certificate in Contemporary Theory in Mental Health Services, and a bachelor's degree in Interdisciplinary Social Science with a concentration in Sociology and a minor in Psychology. I am also pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a concentration in child and adolescent counseling. These experiences have reinforced my interest in the connection between behavioral, emotional, and environmental factors and the importance of creating supportive systems around the individuals we serve.

I would be excited to bring my experience, work ethic, and passion for this field to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I take pride in being dependable, thoughtful, and solutions-focused, and I value creating environments where adolescents and families receive compassionate support and staff members feel encouraged to grow and do their best work. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team that is committed to helping adolescents and their families navigate challenges, build skills, and make meaningful progress.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience align with the needs of your program.

Warm regards,
Josmari Arroyo

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Behavioral Health position. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, program development, and organizational leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise and operational management experience that aligns well with the demands of overseeing behavioral health programs serving adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in program operations, staff supervision, quality improvement, regulatory compliance, and multidisciplinary collaboration. As the founder and Clinical Director of a behavioral health practice, I have directed clinical and administrative operations, developed policies and procedures, managed budgets and performance oversight, and led a multidisciplinary team of seven therapists and two administrative staff. My responsibilities have required balancing clinical quality, operational efficiency, ethical standards, and organizational growth while maintaining a strong commitment to individualized, trauma-informed care.

My experience also includes direct work with youth and vulnerable populations. As a Program Coordinator with Teen Living Programs, I supported children, youth, and young adults experiencing housing instability, coordinated community partnerships, supervised staff and interns, and contributed to program development and resource allocation. These responsibilities strengthened my understanding of the importance of structured, responsive programming, coordinated services, and organizational accountability when supporting young people navigating complex psychosocial challenges.

In addition, my clinical background includes working with individuals experiencing severe and persistent mental illness, trauma, substance use concerns, and other complex behavioral health needs. Through my work in Assertive Community Treatment and other clinical settings, I have developed expertise in crisis intervention, risk management, interdisciplinary coordination, and evidence-based treatment planning. I understand the importance of effective clinical oversight, clear operational protocols, staff development, and collaboration among providers to promote safety, continuity of care, and positive outcomes.

Shamaiah Manriquez
South Florida
331-250-1652
ShamaiahM@Gmail.com

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

I am excited to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Marriage and Family Therapist Intern with experience in mental health and substance use treatment, I am passionate about helping individuals navigate life's challenges, strengthen their relationships, and develop the skills necessary for lasting emotional well-being. I believe my clinical background, compassionate approach, and dedication to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Through my experience working in a Partial Hospitalization Program (PHP), I have had the opportunity to facilitate therapeutic groups, support clients through emotional and behavioral challenges, and create a safe, welcoming environment where individuals feel comfortable expressing themselves. My work has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, encourage meaningful participation, and help clients develop healthier coping skills, improve communication, and better understand themselves.

My education and training in Marriage and Family Therapy have also given me a strong appreciation for the important role family relationships play in an individual's mental health and overall well-being. I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy's emphasis on involving families in the treatment process. I believe that helping adolescents feel heard, understood, and supported while strengthening their family connections can make a meaningful difference in their personal growth and long-term success.

What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to continue developing as a therapist while making a positive impact on the lives of adolescents and their families. I bring empathy, patience, strong interpersonal skills, and a genuine commitment to meeting clients where they are. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, enthusiasm, and dedication to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how I can contribute to your clinical team and the meaningful work you do.

October 23, 2026 

Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and am a recent graduate with my Masters in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Miami. 

As a motivated and compassionate clinician, I am interested in expanding my experience of working with evidence-based treatment modalities. 

My educational experiences have helped me to build my knowledge and experience for working as a registered mental health counseling intern. I have a strong academic background in psychology, as well as a strong interest in working with children and their families to address mental health challenges at an early age, including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression. Through my recent experiences working as a practicum intern at Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and the Institute for Individual and Family Counseling, I was able to establish a strong foundation in conceptualizing cases, applying interventions and building rapport. 

In my previous experience working at Florida International University’s Summer Treatment Program, I had the opportunity to work directly with children and their families, providing support in areas such as emotional regulation, coping skills, and behavioral management. These experiences have provided a good foundation in implementing therapeutic strategies tailored to the unique needs of young children, as well as solidified my interest in child and adolescent mental health. 

I have a passion for working with programs that help to provide low-cost services for a diverse population, as highlighted in my experience working as a practicum intern at the institute for Individual and Family Counseling. I believe that my strong communication skills and dedication will allow for a wonderful learning experience as I continue my work in the field of mental health counseling.  

I have included my resume and look forward to the possibility of discussing further my qualifications. Please feel welcome to contact me at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. 

Respectfully, 
Morgan Reilly

Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. To whom it may concern,

I am writing to express my interest in opportunities focused on human development, family support, behavioral health, and community-based services. My professional background spans early childhood education, in-home childcare, developmental disability support, patient services, and psychiatric care. Through these experiences, I have developed a strong appreciation for the importance of individualized support, compassionate care, and creating environments where individuals and families feel understood and empowered.

My experience in early childhood education and private childcare provided me with a strong foundation in human development, daily caregiving, educational support, and understanding the needs of children and their families. As a Toddler Lead Teacher, Teacher Assistant, and private nanny, I supported children’s developmental milestones through structured routines, age-appropriate activities, and individualized attention. These roles reinforced the importance of consistency, patience, and recognizing that every individual develops and responds to their environment differently.

Additionally, my experience as a Direct Support Professional allowed me to provide individualized care to people with developmental and physical disabilities. My work in healthcare and patient services further strengthened my communication, organizational, and patient-support skills, as well as my understanding of the importance of maintaining privacy, dignity, and respect in care settings.

Over the past year, I have expanded my professional experience into the psychiatric and behavioral health field. I began working as a Behavioral Health Technician with KVC Health Systems in September 2025, supporting children and adolescents in an acute psychiatric setting. I have since transitioned to Discovery Behavioral Health, where I now work with adults. These experiences have broadened my understanding of mental health across different stages of life and strengthened my commitment to supporting individuals as they navigate behavioral health challenges, personal development, and their everyday needs.

My combined background in childhood development, direct care, and behavioral health has shaped my interest in a more comprehensive approach to human services. I recognize that an individual’s well-being is influenced not only by their immediate needs, but also by their relationships, environment, access to resources, and support systems. I am passionate about contributing to services that help individuals and families build stability, strengthen their skills, and access meaningful support in their daily lives.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my diverse experience, adaptability, and commitment to person-centered care to your organization. I am eager to continue growing professionally while contributing to work that promotes individual development, family well-being, and improved quality of life.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and professional goals align with your organization’s mission.

Sincerely,
Alison Barnes

With my professional background in mental health services, experience coordinating patient care, and commitment to helping individuals and families access appropriate treatment, I believe I would be a valuable addition to your team.

In my previous role as a Patient Services Representative for a mental health clinic, I served as a primary point of contact for patients, families, and providers. My responsibilities included answering incoming calls, responding to patient inquiries, coordinating provider schedules, processing referrals and intake paperwork, verifying insurance coverage, and scheduling, rescheduling, and confirming appointments through an electronic medical record (EMR) system. I also assisted patients with questions regarding services, billing, and referrals while ensuring that documentation and administrative procedures were handled accurately and efficiently. This experience strengthened my ability to manage multiple responsibilities, communicate clearly, maintain confidentiality, and help patients navigate the process of accessing mental health care.

Beyond my administrative experience, my work as a Registered Behavior Technician (while providing one-on-one therapy in clinical settings) and Social Service Caseworker (while employed by the state of Alabama) shaped my understanding of the importance of comprehensive, family-centered care. I strongly believe in the value of evidence-based practices grounded in scientific research and data, as well as collaboration among multidisciplinary teams to promote meaningful, lasting patient outcomes. Throughout my work in behavioral health, I have seen the importance of looking beyond an individual’s immediate challenges to consider the broader environment and support system that influence their progress.

I especially appreciate your organization’s commitment to involving families in the treatment process and fostering positive, lasting change. Through my experience as an RBT and social services caseworker, I have developed a strong appreciation for the role families play in supporting continued growth and success. I believe meaningful progress extends beyond the clinical setting and that equipping families with the tools and support to reinforce skills at home and across everyday environments is essential to long-term success. I am passionate about promoting healthy family dynamics, strengthening relationships, and helping establish supportive home environments where individuals and families can continue to thrive. These values closely align with your organization’s comprehensive approach to treatment and reinforce my enthusiasm for the opportunity to contribute to your team.

I understand that connecting adolescents and their families with appropriate treatment requires more than administrative efficiency; it requires compassion, patience, active listening, and a genuine commitment to helping people find the support they need. I would approach every inquiry with professionalism and empathy, recognizing that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be a difficult and vulnerable step for both adolescents and their families. My background has prepared me to communicate with sensitivity, help individuals navigate unfamiliar processes, and coordinate the next steps toward appropriate care.

Additionally, my experience with referrals, insurance verification, intake paperwork, appointment coordination, and electronic medical records has prepared me to manage the detailed responsibilities of this position. I understand the importance of accurate documentation, consistent follow-up, HIPAA compliance, and clear communication among patients, families, and providers. I would bring a dependable, organized, and detail-oriented approach to ensuring that each inquiry receives timely attention and that individuals and families are guided toward the appropriate level of care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in behavioral health, commitment to evidence-based and family-centered care, and dedication to positive patient outcomes would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your admissions team and the individuals and families you serve.


Kaitlyn Uzzell

candidates.cover_letter:
10/27/2026
To whom it may concern:				
	I am writing to you to express interest in the applied position. Recently I graduated from Oregon State University with a BS in Psychology. In my time there I participated in two separate research projects: one as part of a team of undergraduate researchers and the other as a research assistant. I also participated in an extracurricular that has transferable skills to your lab and have an internship with relevant experience. I believe that I would be a great fit for your team and I hope you will consider me as a candidate.
	In my first research project, as part of a team of four undergrads conducting a study I measured the population’s empathy for elderly people. Over the course of 10 weeks my team and I made a research proposal that was approved by an IRB, surveyed over 80 participants, and ran a one-tail t-test on the data. We had regular lab meetings where we reviewed our completed work and discussed our future plans, and briefly checked in with our professor to make sure we were on the right track. All statistics were calculated using JASP or R Studio by all members on the team to ensure redundancy. At the end of the project, we presented our findings at an undergraduate research symposium at Oregon State University. Empathy for the elderly was a particular passion for me, as I have worked as a caregiver for patients with dementia, the majority being the elderly. Seeing and working with these patients has helped me understand cognitive and physical disability on a very personal level. This is a project that I am very proud of. It taught me a lot about time management and working in a research team.
	Additionally, I worked as a research assistant studying university alcohol policy at the Oregon State University's Youth Adjustment Lab with 6 other undergraduate research assistants and a graduate student lead. In this lab I read 35 college alcohol policies and recorded whether or not they met 35 certain conditions onto a spreadsheet. This required attention to detail in the wording of different alcohol policies and ensuring that they met our criteria. My team and I met once a week to discuss various policies and how to categorize them. Together we checked each other’s work and made sure that edge cases were decided fairly. This gave me insight into how school policies were written and how they function. In the process of this research I gained experience in qualitative coding in scientific studies. I also did background literature reviews related to the lab and approached them critically to understand what the authors were attempting to measure, what they actually measured, and what the implications of their findings might be. My team and I presented our research at another Oregon State University undergrad research symposium. This project was useful in developing a deep understanding of research, team decision making, and critical thinking. 
	In my extracurricular time at Oregon State I ran the OSU Gaming Club, where I oversaw a staff of eight officers. We organized 10 different events, 6 days a week, of regular activities. I held weekly meetings with the staff to coordinate expenditures, check in on how the events are progressing, and decide how we can coordinate between the groups. We coordinated with clubs across campus twice a term for large-scale events where we would expect 600 attendees across each event. 
Currently I hold a position as a confidential advocate at the Immigration and Refugee Community Organization (IRCO) working with survivors of domestic violence or sex trafficking. In this position I do confidential data management and processing. I work closely with other advocates to gather data through phone calls to participants in the program and turn it into usable information on an Excel spreadsheet. I also do technical writing for the organization, reviewing projects and writing instructions for future interns at IRCO. 
Finally, I have multiple years of volunteer experience at the Civil Air Patrol, an after school program for teaching youth leadership skills, aerospace knowledge, and emergency service skills. I assisted in running meetings once a week for years educating youth on a variety of topics. In the position I have learned a lot about how to do things like lead a classroom and work through interpersonal issues among adolescents. I believe that education is the most powerful tool we have in empowering our community and this position gave me the tools to do that. 
As you can see, I have a very diverse research background and a long lasting drive for research and people facing roles. In the first I was left largely to my own devices to explore and understand research, in the second I was a part of a well structured team, and last I directed a team. In my internship I was again a part of a team working with confidential advocates. These projects played a large role in developing my knowledge of data science and statistical analysis, critical thinking skills, and approaching problems in new ways with new skills. I have a strong enthusiasm for research and learning new skills. With these qualities which I developed through my research projects, as well as my BS in psychology, I believe I would be an excellent addition to your team. 

Respectfully, 
Jude D. Revier

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than 10 years of experience in service coordination, client care, mental health services, and case management, I have developed a strong commitment to helping individuals and families navigate behavioral health services and access the support they need. I am excited about the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and organizational skills to your team in support of adolescents and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

Through person-centered and trauma-informed approaches, I have supported children, adolescents, adults, couples, and families while contributing to assessments, treatment planning, and coordinated care. My Master of Arts in Marriage and Family Therapy, along with my Master of Business Administration, provides me with a valuable combination of behavioral health knowledge, interpersonal skills, and administrative and organizational strengths.

I understand that connecting adolescents and their families with appropriate treatment requires empathy, professionalism, timely communication, and careful coordination. I would bring a family-centered approach to admissions, along with the ability to build rapport, handle sensitive information with discretion, maintain organized records, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s efforts to connect adolescents and families with appropriate care and support. Thank you for considering my application. Sincerely,

Lynn Coleman

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Mental Health Intake Coordinator position. With my educational background in Psychology and Sociology, hands-on experience in adolescent mental health, current work in mental health case management, and involvement in community recovery services, I am passionate about helping individuals access the support and resources they need to improve their mental health and overall well-being.

My passion for mental health, particularly adolescent mental health and substance use recovery, comes from recognizing how important it is for individuals to feel heard, understood, and supported during some of the most challenging moments of their lives. I believe that everyone deserves compassionate, judgment-free care and the opportunity to receive the help they need, regardless of their circumstances. I am especially passionate about working with adolescents because early intervention, understanding, and access to appropriate resources can make a meaningful difference in a young person's life and future.

Through my experience as a Mental Health Technician at Dayton Children's Hospital, I gained valuable hands-on experience supporting adolescents experiencing mental health and behavioral challenges. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, remain patient in emotionally challenging situations, and recognize the importance of creating a safe and supportive environment. My current role as a Mental Health Case Manager at North Central Mental Health Services has further developed my understanding of behavioral health services, client needs, care coordination, documentation, and connecting individuals with appropriate resources. I also have experience providing Telehealth services, working with Medicaid billing and insurance processes, and helping navigate the systems involved in accessing care.

In addition to my professional experience, volunteering with Hope Spot Recovery Resource Center since 2023 has reinforced my commitment to recovery, community support, and helping individuals find hope during difficult times. My involvement in recovery-focused outreach, including assisting with Hope Fest 2026, has further strengthened my belief in the importance of reducing stigma, building connections, and making support more accessible to individuals and families affected by substance use and mental health challenges. My hands-on exposure to mental health and recovery services has helped me appreciate the importance of meeting people where they are, treating every individual with dignity, and understanding that recovery and healing look different for everyone.

I believe I would be a strong addition to your team because I bring compassion, patience, professionalism, attention to detail, and a genuine commitment to helping others. I understand that the intake process is often a person's first interaction with a mental health provider, and that first impression can have a lasting impact. I would approach every interaction with empathy, respect, and an understanding that reaching out for help can be difficult. I am committed to helping clients feel comfortable sharing their needs, gathering information accurately, maintaining confidentiality, and supporting a smooth connection to appropriate services. I also understand the importance of timely communication, accurate documentation, insurance-related processes, and coordination in ensuring clients can access the care they deserve.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my passion for behavioral health and recovery with my organizational, communication, and client-support skills. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team that values compassionate care, accessibility, and positive outcomes for individuals and families. I am eager to continue growing professionally while making a meaningful difference in the lives of those seeking mental health and recovery support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my education, hands-on experience, and dedication to mental health and recovery could contribute to your organization. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team and helping individuals take an important first step toward receiving the support they need.

Sincerely,
Paige Williams

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager / Team,
I have spent much of my life doing work centered around one simple thing: making sure people feel seen.
Whether I am sitting one-on-one with someone in a behavioral health setting, talking with a participant at a
harm reduction drop-in center, mentoring a young person from the community where I grew up, or helping
someone figure out what comes next, I have learned that people do not always need someone to have all the
answers. Sometimes they need someone who will listen, understand, advocate, and show up.
My experience has taken me through community work, youth mentorship, behavioral health, peer support, and
harm reduction. At Lincoln Hospital, I worked alongside clinical teams while bringing lived experience and the
peer perspective into behavioral health care. At Safe Horizon's Streetwork Project LES, my work expanded into
harm reduction, syringe exchange, participant advocacy, resource connection, housing needs, and creating
health education materials that people could actually understand and use.
Now, I am intentionally taking everything I have learned into the next chapter of my career. My long-term focus
is women's and maternal mental health, particularly the experiences of women of color. I believe women
deserve to be seen and heard at every stage of their lives, especially mothers. I am deeply interested in the parts
of motherhood and womanhood that are often left out of the conversation - the mental load, identity, grief,
isolation, complicated feelings, and the realities women sometimes feel they are not allowed to say out loud.
What I bring is not only professional experience. I bring the ability to connect with people without making them
feel like a case, a diagnosis, or a problem that needs to be solved. I know how to listen, build trust, advocate,
communicate difficult information in a human way, and meet people where they actually are. That is the kind
of work I want to continue doing, and I am looking for an organization where that approach is valued.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience,
perspective, and commitment to a team that values meaningful connection, community, and work that makes a
real difference in people's lives. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.
Warmly,
Ravén Quiñones

Hi,

My name is Kayla Grace, and I'm excited to express my interest in the opportunity at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I recently graduated from Auburn University at Montgomery with my Bachelor of Science in Psychology, and I have experience working with adolescents in both behavioral health and educational settings.

I previously worked as a Behavioral Aide at Safety Net Behavioral Health Care, where I supported adolescents ages 12–18 who were navigating emotional and behavioral challenges. That experience taught me a lot about patience, communication, and the importance of making sure young people feel heard, understood, and supported. I also learned how to remain calm during difficult situations, work alongside other staff members, and recognize when someone may need additional support.

I'm currently a Substitute Teacher, which has allowed me to continue working with young people from different backgrounds and with different needs. One thing I've learned from both positions is that there's no one-size-fits-all approach when it comes to helping people. Sometimes you have to meet them where they are, take the time to understand what's going on, and figure out how you can best support them.

What interests me most about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to continue doing meaningful work in behavioral health while growing professionally. I genuinely enjoy helping people, and I want to build a career where I can make a difference, whether that's through direct support, helping families navigate services, or making sure individuals are connected to the care they need.

I would love the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and willingness to learn to your team. Thank you for taking the time to consider me. I look forward to hearing from you!

Best regards,  
Kayla Grace

MARK A. CHILDS
Columbia, SC 29229
(803) 457-6578
Mark.A.Childs2020@gmail.com


Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, professional experience in behavioral health and substance use treatment services, and 24 years of distinguished service in the United States Air Force, I bring a unique combination of compassion, professionalism, organizational skills, and dedication to helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances.

As the former Lead ADSAP Coordinator at Alpha Behavioral Health Center, I coordinated client intake, screening, assessments, program orientation, case management, referrals, and follow-up services for individuals experiencing substance use challenges. I maintained confidential client documentation, collaborated with treatment professionals and community partners, and helped clients understand their treatment responsibilities and available resources. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate effectively with individuals seeking assistance while ensuring accurate records and continuity of care.

My clinical counseling experience at Transitions Homeless Center and She’s Counseling Center further developed my skills in conducting initial assessments, identifying behavioral health needs, providing supportive counseling, and connecting individuals with appropriate services. Additionally, my experience working with at-risk adolescents at Wil Lou Gray Opportunity School has given me valuable insight into the emotional, behavioral, and family challenges that young people may encounter.

As a retired United States Air Force Master Sergeant, I developed exceptional communication, leadership, accountability, and problem-solving skills. My work supporting military personnel and their families taught me the importance of empathy, discretion, attention to detail, and timely follow-through, especially when assisting individuals facing stressful or emotionally difficult situations.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because I understand that the first conversation with an admissions coordinator can be a critical step toward recovery. I would welcome the opportunity to help adolescents, adults, and their families feel heard, respected, and confident as they explore mental health and substance use treatment options, including Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP).

I am confident that my counseling education, behavioral health experience, client-centered approach, and commitment to professional excellence would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications align with your organization’s mission and how I can contribute to providing compassionate, responsive admissions support.

Sincerely,

Mark A. Childs, MS
Retired United States Air Force Master Sergeant
Master of Science, Clinical Mental Health Counseling

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Social Work degree and hands-on experience supporting adolescents and adults navigating mental health challenges, substance use disorders, eating disorders, and trauma, I bring a strong foundation in behavioral health treatment, compassionate communication, and client-centered care.

In my current role as a Behavioral Health Technician at Eating Recovery Center/Pathlight, I work directly with adolescents receiving residential treatment for eating disorders and co-occurring mental health concerns. I provide emotional support, assist with crisis intervention and de-escalation, monitor patient safety, and collaborate with a multidisciplinary treatment team. This experience has given me valuable insight into the challenges adolescents face during treatment, the importance of family involvement, and the reassurance individuals need when entering a higher level of care.

Additionally, during my social work internship at Counseling Center of Illinois, I supported adults receiving DUI and substance use-related services. My responsibilities included facilitating risk education groups, co-facilitating therapy groups, maintaining accurate client documentation, and utilizing SimplePractice for scheduling and coordinating services. These experiences strengthened my ability to communicate professionally, manage sensitive information, remain organized, and build trust with individuals navigating difficult circumstances.

I see transitioning into admissions as a natural extension of my behavioral health experience. Having worked directly with individuals receiving treatment, I understand how important the admissions process is in shaping their first experience with care. I recognize that families reaching out for treatment may feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or emotionally exhausted, and I know how meaningful it is to have someone who can listen without judgment, provide reassurance, communicate clearly, and help them feel confident taking the next step. My direct-care background allows me to approach these conversations with a genuine understanding of the treatment experience, while my social work education has prepared me to advocate for individuals, assess their needs, and connect them with appropriate support.

I am especially drawn to this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my clinical understanding of behavioral health with my strengths in communication, organization, and relationship-building. I am confident in my ability to learn admissions procedures, coordinate effectively with treatment teams, and provide a positive, compassionate experience for prospective clients and their families.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, dedication, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to discussing how my background and skills align with your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Amy Tehorik, BSW

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a position supporting adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. I believe every young person deserves the opportunity to heal, grow, and build a future beyond the circumstances they have experienced.

My experience at Harbor Heights in Aberdeen strengthened my understanding of the importance of patience, consistency, compassion, and maintaining appropriate boundaries when working with individuals who need support. I recognize that many adolescents face challenges rooted in trauma, unstable family environments, and circumstances beyond their control. These experiences can shape their choices, but they do not have to define their futures.

I believe meaningful change begins with meeting young people where they are, treating them with dignity, and helping them recognize their own strengths and potential. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a supportive environment that encourages emotional growth, recovery, accountability, and lasting positive change.

I am passionate about helping youth understand that their past does not determine their future. I would be proud to bring my compassion, dedication, and commitment to this role and to a team focused on improving the lives of adolescents and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your organization and its mission.

Sincerely,
Miranda Hernandez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. What immediately stood out to me about this opportunity is the chance to be a supportive, reassuring first point of contact for individuals and families who may be reaching out during a difficult or overwhelming time. Throughout my career in behavioral health, healthcare, and child welfare, I have learned how important it is to approach every interaction with compassion, patience, and respect while helping people understand their options and take the next step toward receiving care.

In my experience as an RBT and Student Analyst, I have worked closely with children and their families to support individualized treatment goals, coordinate care, and promote meaningful progress. My responsibilities as a Student Analyst included participating in client intakes and initial assessments, contributing to reassessments and treatment planning, reviewing documentation and behavioral data, supporting parent training, and collaborating with multidisciplinary providers, including speech and occupational therapists. These experiences strengthened my ability to gather relevant information, communicate clearly with families, maintain accurate records, and recognize the importance of connecting each individual with services that meet their needs. I understand that effective care begins well before treatment starts, and I would bring that same thoughtful, family-centered approach to the admissions process.

My previous experience in healthcare administration also aligns closely with the responsibilities of this role. I assisted English- and Spanish-speaking clients with verification of benefits, insurance-related questions, payments, and customer service in a fast-paced environment that required accuracy, organization, and strong communication skills. Additionally, my work as a Child Protective Investigator with the State of Florida strengthened my ability to navigate sensitive conversations, remain composed in challenging situations, gather important information, and communicate with individuals who may be experiencing significant stress. Together, these roles have taught me how to balance empathy with professionalism while ensuring that important details, follow-up, and next steps are not overlooked.

I am drawn to this opportunity because it brings together my experience in behavioral health, my administrative and coordination skills, and my passion for helping individuals and families access the support they need. I am bilingual in English and Spanish, and I value the opportunity to help families feel understood and supported regardless of the language in which they feel most comfortable communicating. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team that recognizes how much a compassionate first conversation can matter, whether that means helping a family navigate treatment options for their teenager or guiding an adult toward appropriate support for mental health and substance use concerns.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, dependability, and genuine commitment to helping others to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my background and skills could contribute to your programs and the individuals and families you serve.

Warm regards,
Josmari Arroyo

candidates.cover_letter:
To Whom It May Concern,

It would be an honor to be the first voice someone hears when taking the first step toward healing. I understand that reaching out for mental health support can be overwhelming, especially for parents seeking help for their children. I strive to be informative, empathetic, and calming while helping others feel heard, seen, and respected during difficult moments.

I hold an Undergraduate Degree in Psychology and a Master of Education, with five years of elementary teaching experience. My background has strengthened my understanding of human behavior, child development, and the importance of recognizing individual needs. I am seeking a second Master’s Degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling as I work toward my long-term goal of becoming a Licensed Professional Counselor.

Although I have not worked professionally in an IOP or PHP setting, I have personal exposure to adolescent and adult treatment programs. More than ten years ago, I was frequently asked to facilitate groups involving cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), and Mindfulness. These experiences deepened my appreciation for mental health support, and I would approach this position with humility, dedication, and a willingness to learn.

One of my strengths is explaining information in an approachable way. I would help families understand their options without overwhelming them with clinical terminology. After all, families should not need a Psychology Degree to understand the next step! They deserve clear answers, patience, and compassion. My experience as a Fourth-Grade Team Lead also strengthened my communication, collaboration, and relationship-building skills. Additionally, I have experience teaching virtually during COVID and providing virtual instruction to students, making me comfortable working with technology and communicating remotely.

I recognize that other applicants may have more direct admissions experience, but I bring a strong foundation in psychology, a genuine passion for mental health, and a sincere desire to help families access care. I would be grateful for the opportunity to learn, contribute to your team, and help make an overwhelming first conversation feel a little less frightening and the next step toward healing a little more hopeful.

Thank you for your time and consideration. 

Sincerely,

Danielle A. Capra, M.Ed.

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for a position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and a professional background supporting children and adolescents with diverse behavioral, emotional, and educational needs, I am passionate about helping young people develop the skills, confidence, and support systems they need to succeed.

In my previous roles as a Registered Behavior Technician, I worked with students in specialized nonpublic school settings, including children whose needs required more individualized support than traditional classroom environments could provide. My background has taught me the importance of patience, consistency, empathy, and meeting individuals where they are. I am especially drawn to opportunities that take a comprehensive approach to wellness and recognize the importance of addressing emotional, behavioral, social, and academic needs together.

In addition to my direct experience supporting students, my management background has strengthened my communication, organization, leadership, and problem-solving skills. I would bring a dependable, compassionate, and collaborative approach to your team, along with a genuine commitment to helping young people recognize their strengths and reach their potential.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and passion for supporting youth align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team and making a meaningful difference in the lives of the adolescents you serve.

Sincerely,
Madison Rimestad

candidates.cover_letter:
Grace A. Friedrich

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology from Widener University, hands-on experience in behavioral health, and a strong background in working with children, families, and individuals with different needs, I believe I would be a valuable addition to your team. I am especially drawn to this opportunity because I want to continue building a career in mental health and help people access the care and support they need.

In my current role as a BHT-ABA with Apex Behavioral Management, I work directly with children and families to support behavioral, emotional, and social development. This role requires patience, clear communication, sound judgment, accurate documentation, confidentiality, and the ability to remain calm and professional in challenging situations. I collect and document behavioral data, follow individualized treatment protocols, support safety and de-escalation, and collaborate with supervisors and other professionals to provide consistent care. These responsibilities have taught me the importance of paying attention to details, following through, and treating every individual and family with dignity and respect.

My previous experience in education and rehabilitation has also strengthened my ability to connect with people from different backgrounds and respond to their individual needs. Additionally, my customer service experience at CVS and in a bagel shop helped me develop communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and customer service skills in fast-paced environments. I understand the importance of making people feel heard, answering questions clearly, staying organized, and creating a positive experience from the first interaction.

I earned my B.A. in Psychology from Widener University in May 2026 with a 3.9 GPA. My education strengthened my understanding of human behavior, mental health, and the factors that influence an individual’s well-being. I am continuing to build on that foundation as I pursue my long-term goal of working in the mental health field. I would be proud to use my education and professional experience to help individuals and families navigate the process of finding appropriate treatment.

What particularly interests me about this position is the opportunity to make a meaningful difference before treatment even begins. Reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can feel overwhelming, especially for a parent seeking help for their teenager or an individual struggling to find the right support. I would approach every interaction with empathy, professionalism, and respect, while helping callers understand their next steps. I also recognize the importance of timely follow-up, accurate records, protecting confidential information, and communicating clearly with clients, families, and providers.

Although my background has primarily focused on direct behavioral health services rather than admissions coordination, I bring a strong foundation in behavioral health, experience with electronic documentation systems, a commitment to confidentiality, and a willingness to learn new systems and procedures. I am eager to build my skills in admissions workflows, intake coordination, and insurance verification while contributing my existing strengths in client support, organization, and communication.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my compassion, reliability, attention to detail, and dedication to mental health care to your team. I am excited about the possibility of helping individuals and families take the first step toward receiving the care they deserve.

Sincerely,

Grace A. Friedrich

candidates.cover_letter:
Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
October 20, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent calls about a struggling teenager, or an adult finally reaches out about their substance use, the first voice they hear matters. I have spent more than 20 years being that voice, and I would love to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator.
My career has been built on admissions, assessment, and referral work. At National Healthcare Associates, I handled inbound referrals from several hospital systems at once for multiple facilities, screened each client against admission criteria, and decided whether to accept, deny, or refer them elsewhere. I verified benefits, secured Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial authorizations, and advocated directly with insurers to keep admissions from stalling. Before that, I spent 17 years as Regional Clinical Admissions Director for Kindred Healthcare, managing the full referral to admission cycle for adults with psychiatric and behavioral needs, including co-occurring drug and alcohol use disorders.
I am used to owning my pipeline without daily direction. At Kindred I independently ran a four-state territory, building relationships with case managers, social workers, and discharge planners both virtually and in person, and following up consistently until every referral had a clear outcome. That work generated enough admissions that the organization opened additional units and a new facility. I am comfortable working in CRM and EMR systems, including EPIC, Navi, and Allscripts, and I keep accurate, HIPAA-compliant records.
I also bring a counselor's foundation. I hold an M.S. in Mental Health Counseling and an M.S.Ed. in School Counseling from Syracuse University, my early clinical work included adolescents in day treatment and residential programs, and I served as board president of YouthHarbor. As a Reiki Master Teacher and owner of Beehive Wellness, I meet people in difficult moments with calm and compassion, which is exactly how I would greet your callers.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families and adults move from that first call to a clear next step. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Keli Scott
